rationale: B wins because it knows where the facts stop: it keeps "Donors, not school districts, are footing the bill for this AI tutor" inside the supplied nonprofit/free/donor facts, while A turns the same point into "while the rest of ed-tech charges per seat," which is an unsupported market claim. A is useful and mostly sharp, especially on the methodology caveat, but it keeps "Khanmigo lands in 30 more districts - what changes inside the classrooms that get it" even though no district, teacher, or classroom access is supplied. B's refused "Inside one pilot district's Khanmigo classrooms" shows better editorial discipline; it would stop a founder from pitching vapor.
gaps_in_A: "while the rest of ed-tech charges per seat" is not in the update. The facts support nonprofit/free/donor-funded; they do not support a category-wide pricing claim.
"set against a market where AI tutoring is typically a paid product" is another unsupported market comparison. A even admits competitor pricing is missing, then uses the contrast anyway.
"Khanmigo lands in 30 more districts - what changes inside the classrooms that get it" is a live angle only if a named district, teacher, or observation access exists. The supplied facts give none.
"one of the largest AI-tutoring deployments" may be directionally plausible from 1 million students, but it is not proven by the update and does not need to be there.
gaps_in_B: "30 districts signing on simultaneously" slightly overstates the update. The facts say Khan Academy is rolling out to 30 more districts, not that all signed at once.

"Khan Academy answers the independent-thinking critics directly" assumes a response posture the facts do not provide. B partly fixes this in proof needed, but the headline should be framed as a challenge, not a fact.
"public-school students" is probably implied by US school districts, but it is still more specific than the supplied wording.
The adoption-trend angle is real, but it needs external context to prove "how fast AI tutoring is moving into public schools" rather than merely "Khan announced a rollout."
